invariants: Upstream ooDialog classes and oodialog-wasm (oodWeb.cls, ooDialog.cls, the tests) are used unchanged. A defect found in oodWeb.cls is proposed to the ooDialog/WASM chat as a patch (see qt6.oodweb-proposals), never fixed in place.
The renderer has no Python, no second process, and no callback into the interpreter from a Qt signal: events are queued and Rexx takes them with oodqt_next.
Each release is a new branch in animatedads/oorexx; a branch is never force-pushed.
Every update states who did the architecture (Tom Dyer), who did the coding, and who wrote the update.

Reports go to TOM in the Rasen Falcon lane python-gate-win-resources. Both the Qt chat and the ooDialog/WASM chat sign in as CLAUDE, and CLAUDE-to-CLAUDE replies are refused, so Tom relays between them.
procedure: Read qt6.current-state for the branch, the oodialog-wasm commit it was tested against, and the results.
Read qt6.architecture and qt6.renderer-contract before changing the renderer.
Run the suite as qt6.testing says before and after a change.
Read qt6.failure-modes before you debug: most failures so far have been differences in geometry or event order between Qt and the page.

The layers, from upstream ooDialog.cls to native/oodqt.cpp.

summary: Upstream ooDialog's Rexx classes run on Linux unchanged. oodialog-wasm (Claude (Fable 5.2)) replaces the Windows DLL with oodWeb.cls, an ooRexx layer that talks to a renderer through one object. In the browser the renderer is a web page. On Linux it is this one: src/js.cls plus a native library, native/oodqt.cpp, built on Qt6 Widgets (Claude (Opus 5.5); architecture Tom Dyer). The renderer is not a rewrite of ooDialog. It implements the page's side of a written contract, RENDERER_CONTRACT.md, and is tested with the browser harness's own tests, unchanged. The code lives in animatedads/oorexx, one branch per release (oodialog-qt6-v0.N), each based on the oodialog-wasm commit it was tested against.
title: ooDialog on Linux is upstream ooDialog, oodWeb.cls, and a Qt6 renderer
